title: Theranos Explained: The $9 Billion Blood Test That Never Worked
description:
In 2014, Theranos was valued at around $9 billion on the promise of dozens of blood tests from a few drops of blood. Then the Wall Street Journal asked whether the technology really worked.

This is the story of Elizabeth Holmes and Theranos: the Stanford dropout who built one of Silicon Valley's most celebrated startups, the famous board, the Walgreens deal, the whistleblowers and the reporter who exposed it, the collapse, the fraud trials of Holmes and Sunny Balwani, and where both stand today.

Sources are listed at the end of the video and include Fortune, Time, NPR, AP, Forbes and U.S. court records. Holmes was convicted of defrauding investors and acquitted on the patient-fraud counts; Balwani was convicted on all counts and has denied wrongdoing. As of November 2026, no decision on Holmes's clemency request had been announced.
